title: Tip Calculation Methodology
overview: Tipping customs vary by country, service type, and dining format. In the US, tipping is customary and often comprises a significant portion of service workers' income.

methods.name: Standard Percentage Method
methods.description: The most common approach: multiply the bill by a percentage based on service quality. Pre-tax amount is traditional, though post-tax has become common.

methods.name: Service-Based Guidelines
methods.description: Different tip percentages based on service quality and type of establishment.

formula.name: Service Tiers
formula.expression:
Poor service: 10-15%
Average service: 15-18%
Good service: 18-20%
Excellent service: 20-25%

methods.name: Split Bill Calculation
methods.description: Dividing total (including tip) among multiple people. Can split evenly or calculate per-person consumption.

formula.name: Even Split
formula.expression: Per Person = (Bill + Tip) / Number of People

limitations: May feel unfair if consumption varied
Doesn't account for who ordered what

sources.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics - Food Service Workers

footnotes: US servers often earn $2.13/hour base wage (federal tipped minimum)
Many countries (Japan, Korea) do not have tipping culture
Some US restaurants have moved to no-tipping models with higher wages
disclaimer: Tipping norms vary by region and establishment. When traveling, research local customs. Some restaurants include gratuity for large parties.
